title: Think Differently Transportation Act
official_summary:
Think Differently Transportation Act

This act requires the National Railroad Passenger Corporation (Amtrak) to include information on compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (ADA) in a required annual report to Congress.

Specifically, Amtrak must incorporate into the annual report an action plan for bringing Amtrak stations into compliance with the ADA as required by a 2020 settlement agreement entered into between Amtrak and the Department of Justice. (Under the agreement, Amtrak committed to complying with the ADA and making intercity rail stations accessible.)

Amtrak must also include a status report on ADA compliance at Amtrak-served stations (based on a station assessment by Amtrak or the party responsible for ADA compliance). For those Amtrak-served stations where Amtrak is not responsible for ADA compliance, Amtrak must include in the report information on the responsible party. Amtrak may meet these requirements by demonstrating that Amtrak took reasonable measures to obtain cooperation from responsible entities.

Further, Amtrak must annually submit the action plan and status report while the settlement agreement is in effect and every five years once the agreement is no longer in effect.

summary.headline: Amtrak must report to Congress each year on its plan and progress for making its train stations accessible under the ADA.
summary.what_it_does: Amtrak must add an ADA action plan and a status report on station accessibility to its annual report to Congress. The plan covers how Amtrak will make stations accessible, as it agreed to do in a 2020 settlement with the Justice Department. For stations where someone other than Amtrak is responsible for ADA compliance, Amtrak must name that party, or show it took reasonable steps to get their cooperation. Reports are due every year while the settlement is in effect, then every five years after it ends.

who_it_affects.how: Amtrak must prepare and submit ADA action plans and station status reports to Congress.
They may get more public information on how accessible Amtrak-served stations are and on plans to improve them.

who_it_affects.group: Station owners other than Amtrak, such as local governments, transit agencies, and freight railroads
who_it_affects.how: They may be named in Amtrak's reports as the party responsible for ADA compliance at stations they control.
They will receive regular reports on Amtrak's progress toward station accessibility.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 23, 2024; the requirements apply to Amtrak's annual reports to Congress, but the summary does not give an exact first deadline.
